newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Silicon Valley state set to be wired.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Silicon Valley state set to be wired.

text.p: Penang, the hub of Malaysia's electronics industry, on Friday launched a project to fully interconnect the island state, officials said.

The PenangNET was "cyber-launched" by Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad from Kuala Lumpur through a high-speed transmission of voice and video that allowed interaction between him and his audience in Penang, organisers for the launch said in a statement.

The project is a public-private sector initiative to fully interconnect the island which houses Malaysia's "Silicon Valley", comprising over 700 factories including some of the world's biggest electronics product makers.

PenangNET hopes to connect the island with high-speed telecommunications infrastructure and applications "that will enable the state government, industries and individuals to tap the full power of the digital economy", the statement said.
The project will include broadband transmission of an initial high speed of up to 155 megabits per second through an all fibre optic network.
The project will also enable Penangites to have high-speed access to the Internet via the World Wide Web, the statement said.

Penang Network Services Sdn Bhd, the firm behind PenangNET, is a joint venture between THB Asia Connect Sdn Bhd, a unit of Tongkah Holdings Bhd, Bina-Sat Com Network Sdn Bhd and Public Packages Holdings Bhd.
